llm_reasoning.analyte_preparation_explanation: Vitamin C is assumed to be solid L-ascorbic acid, molecular weight 176.12 g/mol. It is dispensed directly into the experiment vial as a separate analyte solid and dissolved together with KCl in water. The fresh solution should be measured immediately after mixing and nitrogen purge because dissolved ascorbic acid is susceptible to air oxidation.
assumptions: Vitamin C refers to L-ascorbic acid rather than sodium ascorbate or another Vitamin C formulation.
Potassium chloride is available as a dry solid in Quantos cartridge position 1.
L-ascorbic acid is available as a dry solid in Quantos cartridge position 2 and can be accurately dispensed at the planned 1.233 mg mass.
Water is available as a pump-compatible solvent on syringe-pump channel 1.
The stated final volume is the platform nominal preparation volume defined by dispensing 7.000 mL water; small solute-volume effects are neglected in the concentration calculation.
Nitrogen is connected and available to the electrochemical substation purge function.
The gold working electrode will be polished, washed, dried, and inspected according to the substation procedure before measurement.
The pH measurement capability will be used before and after the CV test; no buffer is added so the measured pH is expected to be mildly acidic and may change after electrochemical oxidation.

concentration_calculations.calculation_explanation: Required moles = 0.100 mol/L x 0.007000 L = 0.000700 mol. Theoretical mass = 0.000700 mol x 74.5513 g/mol = 0.05218591 g = 52.18591 mg. The planned Quantos mass is rounded to 52.193 mg. Actual concentration based on the planned mass and nominal 7.000 mL preparation volume is (0.052193 g / 74.5513 g/mol) / 0.007000 L = 0.100013 mol/L.

Required moles = 0.001000 mol/L x 0.007000 L = 0.000007000 mol. Theoretical mass = 0.000007000 mol x 176.12 g/mol = 0.00123284 g = 1.23284 mg. The planned Quantos mass is rounded to 1.233 mg. Actual concentration based on the planned mass and nominal 7.000 mL preparation volume is (0.001233 g / 176.12 g/mol) / 0.007000 L = 0.00100013 mol/L.

llm_reasoning.constraint_validation_summary: The plan uses two solid cartridges, below the maximum of eight. Each solid mass is below the 200 mg maximum per Quantos cartridge. One compatible liquid solvent is used, below the four-channel limit. Water volume is 7.000 mL, below the 10 mL vial limit and exactly compatible with the 7 microliter dispensing increment because 7000 microliters equals 1000 increments of 7 microliters. One electrochemical slot is used, below the maximum of three parallel slots. Potassium chloride and L-ascorbic acid are represented as solids and are assigned to Quantos cartridges; water alone is assigned to the liquid pump. The required physical prerequisites are that cartridge position 1 contains potassium chloride, cartridge position 2 contains L-ascorbic acid, and water is available on pump channel 1.
llm_reasoning.drying_explanation: No drying step is required because no analyte is deposited on the working electrode.
llm_reasoning.electrode_deposition_explanation: No electrode deposition is performed because Vitamin C is characterized as a dissolved analyte in the electrolyte.
llm_reasoning.electrolyte_preparation_explanation: Dispense 52.193 mg potassium chloride from Quantos cartridge position 1 into one experiment vial. Dispense 1.233 mg L-ascorbic acid from Quantos cartridge position 2 into the same vial. Dispense 7.000 mL water from pump channel 1. Mix with the vial stir bar for 180 seconds until no visible solids remain. Purge the homogeneous solution with nitrogen for 300 seconds, then measure and record pH immediately before CV. The nominal preparation volume is 7.000 mL; concentrations are reported using this platform-defined solution volume.
llm_reasoning.parameter_selection_logic: A 0.10 M KCl aqueous supporting electrolyte provides adequate ionic conductivity while being electrochemically simple in the selected potential region. A 1.00 mM L-ascorbic acid concentration is sufficient to produce a measurable oxidation response while limiting excessive gold-electrode fouling. The potential scan from -0.10 V to +0.70 V versus Ag/AgCl is intended to include the anodic oxidation of ascorbic acid on gold while avoiding an unnecessarily extended positive-potential region where gold oxide formation becomes more significant. A 50 mV/s scan rate and 5 mV increment provide an initial characterization scan with practical acquisition time and potential resolution. Three cycles permit observation of possible electrode conditioning or signal loss caused by oxidation-product adsorption. MICROAMPS200 is selected as a conservative current range for a 1 mM analyte at a gold electrode; the expected current is assumed to be below 200 microamps.
llm_reasoning.selected_mode_explanation: The requested experiment requires Vitamin C to remain dissolved in the supporting electrolyte during cyclic voltammetry. Therefore, analite_in_electrolite is selected. No working-electrode deposition or drying operation is required.

metadata.description: Characterization of dissolved Vitamin C (assumed L-ascorbic acid) by cyclic voltammetry in freshly prepared 1.00 mM Vitamin C and 0.10 M KCl aqueous electrolyte using a gold working electrode, platinum counter electrode, and Ag/AgCl reference electrode. The sample is nitrogen-purged to reduce dissolved-oxygen reduction and Vitamin C oxidative degradation prior to measurement.
metadata.experiment_name: Cyclic Voltammetry of Vitamin C in 0.10 M KCl on Gold
metadata.user_prompt: Perform a cyclic voltammetry experiment to characterize Vitamin C as an analyte dissolved in the electrolyte. The Vitamin C should be prepared in the electrolyte and measured using the electrochemical substation. Use the available gold working electrode, platinum counter electrode, and Ag/AgCl reference electrode. Select appropriate electrolyte composition, Vitamin C concentration, CV parameters, mixing/preparation steps, and safety precautions based on the capabilities and constraints provided in the system context. The resulting experiment must be directly executable by the CVLab platform.

cross_contamination_risks: Ascorbic acid oxidation products can adsorb on the gold working electrode and alter subsequent voltammograms.
Residual chloride electrolyte or Vitamin C solution on electrodes can contaminate later experiments.
Use electrode washing and drying after the measurement and polish the gold electrode before this measurement.
handling_precautions: Load L-ascorbic acid and potassium chloride cartridges using appropriate laboratory PPE, including safety glasses, lab coat, and gloves.
Avoid generating or inhaling solid dust during cartridge loading.
Prepare the Vitamin C solution immediately before the CV measurement and minimize exposure to air and light because ascorbic acid oxidizes over time.
Use the platform nitrogen purge function only with adequate laboratory ventilation.
Polish, wash, and dry the gold working electrode before the experiment to reduce contamination and surface-fouling artifacts.
Measure electrolyte pH immediately before and after the CV test using the available pH measurement capability.
hazards: L-ascorbic acid is a low-hazard organic acid but its powder may cause eye, skin, or respiratory irritation.
Potassium chloride is low hazard but should not be inhaled as dust or ingested.
The prepared electrolyte is mildly acidic due to dissolved ascorbic acid.
Nitrogen purging can create a localized oxygen-deficient atmosphere if used outside suitable ventilation.
waste_disposal: Collect the post-CV Vitamin C/KCl electrolyte as aqueous electrochemical waste according to local laboratory procedures.
Do not return used electrolyte to reagent reservoirs or reuse it for another measurement.
Rinse the gold working electrode, platinum counter electrode, and Ag/AgCl reference electrode according to platform procedures after measurement.
